subject: Re: Luminate Health — dedicated pool sizing: precision vs context tradeoffs
messages:
From: Maya Kapoor <maya.kapoor@luminatehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Joel Turner <joel.turner@luminatehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing — model memory questions

Hey Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Joel and I ran a quick internal pass and have two follow-ups that will determine whether we go Reserved or Hosted with burst capacity. High level:

- Our key inference path is a clinical summarization flow using the Lume-med-70B model variant (native 32k context for notes ingestion). Typical request: 12–20k input tokens + 2–4k generated tokens.
- We will need PII redaction steps that run in-stream (adds ~300 tokens of KV use per request).

Questions for sizing:
1) We heard quantized int8 lowers memory substantially but impacts some rare token probabilities — what’s the realistic change in GPU footprint for 70B @32k vs 16k context if we move from fp16 -> int8 or int4?
2) If we adopt a mixed strategy (fp16 for QA/critical outputs, int8 for plain summarization), can Redwood route different requests to different variants without extra effort on our side?
3) What headroom should we budget for autoscale and tail-latency during peak clinical batch windows (7–9am ET)?

We attached a short export of our sample logs (token distributions + 95th pct lengths). Would appreciate a one-page sizing guidance we can take to procurement.

Thanks,
Maya Kapoor
VP, Product
Luminate Health
Attachments: 20261120-luminate-initial-kv-metrics.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing — model memory questions
Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clear asks and the sample token distribution. I looped in Marcus from our capacity team and Aditya (solutions) so we can give you both a practical sizing recommendation and how that maps to deal economics. Quick answers up front:

- Yes — quantization materially reduces GPU memory but the savings depend on KV cache pressure (long context hurts).
- Redwood can route by request type to model variants (we call it "policy-based routing") so your mixed-precision strategy is supported without changes to your app.
- For headroom, we typically ask for a target p95 latency SLA (e.g., 1.2s for small gen, 3s for 4k+ outputs). I'll ask Marcus for a concrete GPU count and preferred autoscale cushion for your observed peaks.

Marcus — can you take the attached token profile and produce: (A) device-memory per instance for Lume-med-70B at 32k vs 16k (fp16, int8, int4), (B) recommended reserved GPU count for steady baseline (30 RPM, 95th token length 18k request), and (C) burst sizing for 3x peak. Please include assumptions (batch size, sequence kv memory per token, kv offload options) and list any operational tradeoffs (e.g., throughput vs tail latency).

Maya/Joel — we’ll put a 1-pager in Drive by EOB Monday.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Maya Kapoor <maya.kapoor@luminatehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing — model memory questions
Hi all —

I ran a quick sizing sweep based on the provided distribution and internal performance models. See summary below; I attached the raw spreadsheet with per-shape memory numbers. Assumptions: Lume-med-70B dense architecture, KV size ~= 96 bytes/token (post-kernel), base model params memory (fp16) ~= 70B * 2 bytes ~= 140GB (sharded), working memory / optimizer not relevant for inference, and we consider two runtime options: full in-GPU KV (low latency) and KV offload to NVMe (lower memory per GPU but higher p95). Batch target: 1–2 concurrent requests per stream; target throughput 30 RPM baseline; p95 latency SLO budgets as Soojin suggested.

Memory per-device (effective resident model + cache) estimates:
- 32k context, fp16: ~220GB resident (requires distributed with 4x 80GB A100 equivalents or sharded across 8x 48GB GPUs with NVLink aggregation).
- 32k context, int8: ~150GB resident (approx -30% vs fp16 for weights + modest KV compression).
- 32k context, int4: ~120GB resident (further -20% vs int8 but with some degradation in tail-case probabilities).
- 16k context, fp16: ~160GB resident.
- 16k context, int8: ~110GB resident.

What this means for reserved pool sizing (steady baseline: 30 RPM, 95th token length 18k):
- If Luminate wants consistent low p95 and full in-GPU KV: recommend reserving capacity equivalent to 6 x 80GB-class GPUs (fp16, 32k) to handle concurrency headroom and autoscale buffer.
- Mixed strategy (int8 for summarization, fp16 for high-fidelity redaction): reserve a baseline of 4 x 80GB-class GPUs (int8-primary) + 2 x 80GB-class as hot standby fp16 nodes for critical request routing. That reduces committed spend by ~30% while preserving fidelity where it matters.
- If you accept NVMe KV offload for cold-prefixes: you can compress baseline further (approx another 15% GPU reduction) but expect p95 penalty ~200–400ms depending on NVMe bandwidth and PCIe gen.

Autoscale & tail protection:
- For clinical 7–9am surges, plan for 3x baseline burst capacity. If baseline 4 GPUs (mixed) -> burst to 12 GPUs; plan for warm-up cold starts by staggering scale events (we can support pre-warmed spare instances).

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Int4 gives the best density but requires per-operator validation vs your eval set (we’ve seen rare hallucination shifts in redaction-critical tokens). Recommend a phased rollout: int8 -> A/B test -> int4 on low-risk routes.
- Routing: Redwood policy routing can send requests by metadata flags ("redaction=true") and will pick the fp16 variant automatically. No app changes required beyond adding a header/flag.

I attached the detailed spreadsheet with per-GPU memory rows and latency tradeoffs. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the numbers.

- Marcus
Principal Capacity Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: 20261121-marcus-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx

Soojin / Marcus / Aditya,

Thanks for the fast turnaround. This is precisely the level of detail procurement wanted. Two quick clarifications before I share with our finance lead:

1) Can you convert the mixed-strategy recommendation into monthly committed GPU hours and a dollar estimate (ballpark) so procurement can see the delta between 4 committed + 2 hot-standby vs 6 committed (all fp16)?
2) For the phased rollout we’ll likely want a canary on ~5% traffic for int4. Does Redwood autoscaler support weighted routing during rollout windows and metrics to detect subtle QA regressions?

If you can drop a short cost delta and confirm the canary capabilities I’ll attach to the SOW and loop Legal.
Appreciate it —
Joel
